criteria.passage: I would tell the customer that the issue is being looked at and reassure them that it will be fixed soon, because I wouldn’t want to leave them frustrated with an open-ended answer.
criteria.rationale: This clearly states how the candidate would communicate the situation in understandable terms.

criteria.passage: Even if the technical team hasn’t confirmed the cause yet, I’d commit to getting it resolved quickly and let them know I expect a fix in the next day or two.
criteria.rationale: The candidate makes an unsupported promise and provides a specific resolution timeframe despite explicitly noting the cause is unconfirmed, which materially contradicts justified expectation-setting.

criteria.passage: I’d probably tell them I’ll check back if anything changes
criteria.rationale: This establishes a follow-up mechanism by indicating the candidate will check back when there is an update.

annotation.annotation_notes: Criterion C1 is satisfied by a plain-language status update. Criterion C2 is negatively evidenced because the candidate commits to a quick fix and a next-day-or-two timeframe without support. Criterion C3 is satisfied by a stated follow-up plan, though it is limited to changes/updates.
